text:
sophia: Heads-up — onboarding neo9b-int4 (converted from gemma-style export). Running the usual eval sweep and seeing a small but consistent prefix drift vs fp16 baseline after ~40 tokens. not catastrophic but repros across prompts.

amir: Can you paste the conversion command + quant flags?

sophia: sure — used the conversion pipeline we put in infra, then int4 static per-tensor with rowwise fold. command: 

```
python convert.py --src model.gem --dst neo9b.pt --rotary-format=per-head --quant=int4 --blocksize=128
```

sophia: quick log snippet: 

```
[INFO] kv_cache warmup ok
[WARN] rotary_scale mismatched for head 3: expected 1.0 got 0.998
[DEBUG] first 64 toks alignment score: 0.9987
```

nina: hmm that rotary_scale warning stands out. which rotary mode did you pick? per-head vs shared? some exporters default to a scaled freq.

sophia: per-head (we wanted to preserve headwise freqs). conversion noted per-head in the header.

oliver: Could be the quant packer changing small float deltas that amplify in rotary trig functions. Did you try a float16 warmup run (no quant) and then quantize-in-place?

sophia: I ran two experiments: (A) fp16 baseline, (B) int4 static as above, (C) post-quant with fake-quant warmup (simulate quant noise during fine-tune). Results: B shows prefix drift ~0.6% log-prob delta by token 50; C reduces drift to ~0.2% but still not zero.

amir: Important: are token ids identical between gemma tokenizer and our neo onboard tokenizer? sometimes a sentinel mapping or ZWJ normalization shifts ids and you only notice after long context.

sophia: checked — mapping identical for first 50k tokens. differences only in rare combine diacritics (not in these prompts).

dev-bot: perf-bench results uploaded: https://internal/redwood/bench/1759812345/neo9b-quant-sweep (summary: latency ok, mem savings 3.2x)

nina: can you run a quick KV-cache consistency check? feed same prompt twice, compare cached keys for first 8 heads. snippet: 

```python
# compare k/v matrices after token 16
k1, v1 = get_kv(model_int4, prompt)
k2, v2 = get_kv(model_fp16, prompt)
assert close(k1[:, :8], k2[:, :8], atol=1e-3)
```

sophia: running now. quick result: heads 0-4 close, heads 5-7 drift ~1.2e-2 on average (above atol).

oliver: that aligns with the rotary_scale warning on head 3 earlier — drift concentrated in certain head groups. maybe the exporter packs head order differently (interleaved vs grouped).

amir: action items: 1) try conversion with rotary-format=shared to see if per-head mismatch is the culprit, 2) run int4 with different quant bucket sizes (blocksize 64 vs 128), 3) run KV compare with per-head repro dumps.

sophia: I started 1 and 2. preliminary: shared-rotary conversion removed the warning and reduced head drift to <3e-3, and blocksize 64 helped too but not as much as switching rotary mode.

nina: interesting — does shared rotary change absolute freq scaling? we might need to adapt our runtime kernel for per-head rotary tables when running quantized weights.

amir: also check attention proj order (q/k/v layout). if exporter switched proj order (qkv vs qkv_per_head) it could shift how we apply sin/cos tables.

sophia: adding a small repro script to the bench job with head dumps + token sequences. linking here when ready.

oliver: thanks — if shared rotary fixes it we can either: a) tweak converter to normalize per-head scales post-quant, or b) enable shared rotary as a conversion-time fallback for int4. prefer (a) if it preserves expressivity.

sophia: agreed. prioritizing a normalization patch that rescales per-head rotary tables to match post-quant weight norms. will open PR and attach the bench artifact.

amir: great. once PR is up ping me and I'll run the regression suite across our eval set (summarization + codegen + chat). :thumbsup:

sophia: will do — thanks all. (reaction :eyes:)
